titles: Proaction Uses Codex For 60% Sales Jump
AI Demo Tool: 60% More Sales For Proaction
title: Codex: 60% Sales Boost, 75+ Hrs Saved
description:
Proaction achieves a 60% sales increase and saves over 75 hours with the power of OpenAI's Codex. Discover how this AI tool is revolutionizing fleet management sales demos. We dive into how customized interactive demos are built and delivered, freeing up engineering resources and directly impacting the bottom line. See how non-technical users can now create sophisticated sales tools, a massive shift from relying on engineers. This isn't just about saving time; it's about closing more deals faster by showing prospects exactly what they need, built with their own data. Learn about the broader implications for software development and sales processes. #AI #OpenAI #Codex #FutureOfWork #SalesTech #Productivity

Source: https://openai.com/index/proaction

synthesis_claim: The ability for non-technical sales teams to autonomously generate hyper-personalized, interactive product demonstrations using AI fundamentally shifts the sales paradigm from product explanation to collaborative solution co-creation, directly accelerating deal cycles and resource allocation.

scenes.narration: This week's most impactful tech development, impacting sales and engineering workflows, flew surprisingly under the radar. We're talking about a company that leveraged AI to not only boost sales by a massive 60% but also reclaim over 75 hours of work. Stick around to understand exactly how.
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: The company is Proaction, which builds software for businesses managing vehicle fleets. Their challenge? Demonstrating how their platform fits each unique fleet operation. This meant custom demos, which traditionally ate up precious engineering time.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: Before, if a prospect needed a tailored look at the software, a non-technical person like the COO had to pull engineers away from their core work. This bottleneck meant relying on generic presentations instead of showing real value.
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: That's where OpenAI's Codex came in. It flipped the entire sales process. Now, the COO can create these customized, interactive demos himself, in about 30 to 45 minutes each, a task that used to require significant engineering hours.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: He's now producing four to six of these custom demos monthly. According to OpenAI's blog, this saves an estimated 40 to 60 engineering hours every single month. That's a huge chunk of capacity freed up.
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: The magic happens after a sales call. Codex is fed call recordings, prospect emails, and any shared spreadsheets. It then builds an HTML demo environment that mirrors Proaction's product, but critically, using the prospect's own fleet data.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: Imagine a prospect seeing their own trucks or machinery on screen, arranged exactly how their business operates. They can directly point out what needs tweaking, effectively co-building the solution without any engineers in the room.
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: This personalized approach gives prospects a tangible reason to move forward. Proaction reports that the rate of deals progressing from initial contact to solution development, bypassing the usual 'nurture' stage, has increased by 50% to 60%.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: But here's the problem: we often hear about AI saving time. Is this just another efficiency play, or does it fundamentally change how companies operate and sell?
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: It's more than just efficiency. If Proaction's engineers built these demos, it would take them about 10 hours each. So, four to six demos a month means 40 to 60 hours saved from engineering. But the impact doesn't stop there.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: When a prospect becomes a customer, those custom demos become a visual reference for the engineers. This drastically cuts down on back-and-forth questions, streamlining the transition from sales to production.
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: Proaction even used Codex to build a customer solution center. Here, prospects can explore tailored workflows and review sales materials, empowering them to articulate their needs clearly before engineers even get deeply involved.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: What we're seeing here isn't just a tool for sales. Codex plugins integrate with tools like Granola, Gmail, Slack, and GitHub. This means Colin can pull call transcripts, create tasks in Linear, and update HubSpot opportunities, all within Codex.
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: He even set up automated sales updates by reviewing recent calls. Before, this involved jumping between countless tabs and manual data entry. Now, it's a more unified, descriptive workflow.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: This story highlights a fundamental shift: AI empowering non-technical roles to perform highly technical tasks, not just for efficiency, but for direct revenue generation and improved product development handoffs. It collapses silos between sales, support, and engineering.
scenes.speaker: a

scenes.narration: The strangest part? This level of AI integration in sales and product visualization, leading to such concrete business results, is still not the norm for most companies. It's a clear indicator of where the future of interactive sales and product development is heading.
scenes.speaker: b

scenes.narration: So, Proaction leveraged AI to build custom demos on the fly, boosting sales significantly and saving engineer time. This is a powerful example of how AI can fundamentally reshape business operations. What if your sales team could build custom product demos instantly?
scenes.speaker: a
